facts.statement: The genus Feitianius was named and described in 2015 by a team of seven researchers including Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Feitianius paradisi was named and described by Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Li Daqing, Matthew C. Lamanna, Wang Min, Jerald D. Harris, Jessie Atterholt and You Hailou.

facts.statement: The genus name Feitianius is derived from the feitian, a flying nymph from Buddhist mythology.
facts.quote: The generic name has been derived from the feitian, a flying apsara or nymph from Buddhist mythology.

facts.statement: The thighbone of Feitianius measured twenty-seven millimetres in length.
facts.quote: A hint of the size of Feitianius is given by the length of the thighbone, twenty-seven millimetres.

facts.statement: Feitianius is unique among known relatives for having tail plumage with three distinct feather types.
facts.quote: A single unique feature was established for Feitianius: the tail plumage contains three distinct feather types whereas all known relatives have tails with a single type of feather.

facts.statement: The tail feathers of Feitianius were considered unlikely to have had an important aerodynamic function.
facts.quote: It was considered unlikely that the tail feathers had an important aerodynamic effect.

facts.statement: Feitianius lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Feitianius was placed in the Enantiornithes in 2016.
facts.quote: Feitianius was in 2016 placed in the Enantiornithes.

facts.statement: Feitianius belongs to the parent group Enantiornithes.

rejected.statement: The species name paradisi means 'from paradise' in Latin, referencing the sexual dimorphism in tail feathers of birds-of-paradise.
rejected.quote: The specific name means 'from paradise' in Latin and refers to the similar sexual dimorphism in the tail feathers of birds-of-paradise.
